NgraceChangeDesignContext.Rationale:
This bundle is a small follow-on teaching repair on the current-only CLI track. The normative source of truth is `spec.xml`; nothing here adds a requirement, and every binding obligation is repeated in the spec's acceptance criteria and scope.
The defect is a phase contradiction inside one rule set. `ngrace-plan` rule 19 told the planner to drive "the full CI in a faithful post-close copy at plan time", while rule 20 reserves the full CI-equivalent verification for close time under the outer `--assertions final --run-commands` gate. The increment that added the rule-19 demand and the commit that added rule 20 both survive in history; this repair resolves the contradiction by keeping what each rule was for. PLAN still proves that its narrow commands and structural assertion probes can run, on disposable complete projects, in the state each task leaves and in a close-shaped copy where the evidence depends on it. The full CI run is not a PLAN instrument. EXECUTE owns two distinct CI activities: the executor's single outer selected `--assertions final --run-commands` gate on the active approved bundle, whose full CI-equivalent leaves are `bun run validate:ci`, `bun run validate:cli`, and `bun run release:check`; and authority/Luna's independent rehearsal of the sanctioned apply/archive on a faithful copy, followed by those same three direct commands on the faithfully applied and archived copy. The independent post-close run is not the active outer final gate: an applied copy is not reapproved and no active status is fabricated. Prototype, planted-violation, restoration, approval, fingerprint, lifecycle, and command-attribution obligations are untouched.
The same rule carried a second stale statement: that a faithful post-close copy must carry `.ngrace/scratch` read-only or `review.confidently-wrong` fires on archived plan baselines. The review read boundary moved: it discovers active `plan.xml` files and derives the bundle location before opening any plan content (`src/review/core.ts:504-518`), so an unrelated archived plan is opaque history and its `MustExist` buffer path is never evaluated. The claim must be recast, not mechanically deleted, because the underlying instruction is still useful: a faithful copy must carry the inputs the selected evidence actually declares — the repository state, the applicable VCS state, and the ignored/untracked inputs the run depends on. What goes away is the named archive-baseline symptom and any temptation to add an archive reader or to hard-code this repository's record pipeline into the published skill.
The teaching instrument is part of the deliverable, not an afterthought: `check-taught-rules` pins one load-bearing token per taught rule, and the stale-cause needle at `scripts/check-teaching-surface.ts:456` currently pins `review.confidently-wrong`. It must move to the recast sentence, and a positive phase needle plus a negative stale-claim guard must make the corrected contract fail-closed if a later edit regresses it. Finally, a `SKILL.md` edit moves the measured footprint; the strict numeric pins in `src/test-support/token-accounting.test.ts` and the `README.md` cell are re-measured with the unchanged instrument and transcribed — the relation is normative, the figure is not.
The reviewed conceptual diagrams below are explanatory. They describe the phase contract, not new implementation classes, and they add no SPEC-stage work. Every binding behaviour is repeated in the spec's acceptance criteria.

Alternatives.Alternative: Keep the full-CI-at-PLAN sentence and weaken rule 20 instead. Rejected: it would move the whole CI-equivalent verification, and the single outer final gate that owns it, into planning; the increment was introduced against the predecessor's close-time-only criterion, and the original purpose is served by narrow feasibility work plus EXECUTE-final evidence.

Delete the faithful-copy guidance wholesale when its scratch example became obsolete. Rejected: the generic requirement is still load-bearing — a copy missing declared inputs, VCS state, or ignored/untracked inputs produces evidence the selected commands cannot evaluate — so the sentence is recast, not removed.

Add an archive reader or re-introduce archive-aware review teaching so the old scratch claim becomes true again. Rejected: it reopens historical-schema compatibility the current-only policy withdraws, and hard-codes this repository's record pipeline into a published skill.

Fix the teaching text and leave the checker needle on `review.confidently-wrong`. Rejected: the needle would then require the false causal claim to remain, and no guard would protect the corrected phase contract.

Project the post-edit footprint figures into the spec now. Rejected: a projected figure expires the moment the edit lands (F272); the spec states the relation — pins and README cell equal the measured final canonical totals — and the implementation transcribes the measurement.

DeferredDecisions.Decision: The exact replacement needles and the exact recast sentences are plan/implementation detail. The binding requirements are that a positive `ngrace-plan` must_do needle pins PLAN-does-not-run-CI / CI-is-EXECUTE-close-time, that a negative guard reddens on the removed obsolete claim, and that the stale-cause needle no longer depends on `review.confidently-wrong`.

Whether the negative guard is a new constant on the existing stale-claim walk or a new small check function is plan detail; it must stay inside the two already-scoped checker files and add no runtime export or dependency.
The post-change `skillTextLines().total` and `.totalBytes` are measured through the shipped instrument after implementation; no figure is projected here.

Phase-contract guard scenario on disposable fixtures. A planted `ngrace-plan` SKILL.md that instructs running the full CI at PLAN, or that restores the scratch-cause claim, reddens the negative guard and names the file; a clean pair of trees passes. A planted SKILL.md that drops the corrected phase sentence reddens the positive `ngrace-plan` must_do needle and names the missing token. Both directions are driven, and the real canonical and packaged trees pass.

Faithful-copy scenario. A planner assembles a disposable, complete close-shaped copy carrying the selected record's declared inputs/dependencies, applicable VCS state, and necessary ignored/untracked inputs; the narrow verification commands and relevant structural assertion probes evaluate against that copy without running the full CI. The full CI-equivalent verification belongs to EXECUTE and has two distinct activities. The executor runs the active approved bundle's single outer selected `--assertions final --run-commands` gate, whose full CI-equivalent leaves are the direct package commands `bun run validate:ci`, `bun run validate:cli`, and `bun run release:check`. Authority/Luna then independently rehearse the sanctioned apply/archive on a faithful copy of the delivered state and run those same three commands on the faithfully applied and archived copy. The independent post-close run is not the active outer final gate: it does not reapprove an applied copy or fabricate active status.

Preservation-instrument scenario on a complete disposable Git fixture. Guard A inventories base Git paths/blob bytes and actual filesystem entries under both `.ngrace/changes/archive` and `docs/plans/archive`: clean, ordinary and staged byte changes in either tree, a mode change, a masked (`--assume-unchanged` / `--skip-worktree`) byte change, an untracked or ignored addition under an existing root, and a new root in either tree; the exact sanctioned own archive arrival passes; each mutation is restored and raw restoration equality is checked. Guard B scans all base-tracked paths including both archive trees except the six allowed product paths and the exact own active/archive directories: clean and the six-path/own-close controls pass; an outside tracked ordinary or staged byte change, a staged addition, a deletion, a type/mode change, and a masked byte change each fail; each mutation is restored. Both guards read exit codes directly and fail closed on a missing base or a failed Git or filesystem read, and neither parses archive XML, schema, or content.

Parity and footprint scenario. The canonical `skills/ngrace/ngrace-plan/SKILL.md` and its packaged mirror are byte-identical; `skillTextLines()` measures the edited canonical tree, and the strict test pins and the README measurement cell are transcribed from that measurement so all three agree. No projected figure is written into the spec.
